notes: Existing payloads are reused verbatim only when course code, unit/topic alignment and departmental flag match.

subjects.name: APPLIED CHEMISTRY
subjects.objective: To study fundamentals of chemistry, make students capable of understanding and learning the concepts of electrochemistry, study basics of organic chemistry, study the synthesis, properties and applications of polymers used in our day-to-day life, study the applications of chemistry in our day-to-day life
course_outcomes: Understand the concepts of fundamental of chemistry and organic chemistry
Will be aware of the basics of reaction mechanism and structure & stability of reacting constituents
Obtain the information regarding the electromotive force and cells
Understand the use of chemistry in our day-to-day life
Identify various electrochemical systems for use in domestic and industrial settings

allSyllabusUnits.title: Basic Concepts of Chemistry
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Importance of Chemistry, Nature of matter, classification based on physical state, classification based on chemical structure, Physical quantities, atomic mass, molecular mass, molar mass and mole concept, Atomic number, atomic mass, isotope, isobar and isotone. Bohr's atomic model, Quantum numbers, shape of s, p, d and f orbitals, rules of electron arrangement in orbitals.

allSyllabusUnits.title: General Organic Chemistry
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, tetravalency of carbon, hybridization, sp, sp2 and sp3 hybrid orbitals with examples, functional groups, IUPAC nomenclature of organic compounds, inductive effect, main types of organic reactions.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Electromotive Force
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Types of electrochemical cells and examples, Half- cell, Reversible and irreversible cell, Convention sign, Types of electrodes, cell reactions, Representation of cell, emfof cell, emf series. Thermodynamicderivation of Nernst equation. Standard cells. Half-cells/electrodes, different types ofelectrodes (with examples). Standard electrode potential (IUPAC convention) andprinciples of its determination. Types of cells: electrolytic, galvanic and concentration cells

allSyllabusUnits.title: Polymers
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, classification of polymers, industrial manufacturing, properties and uses of some important polymers: Polythene, Teflon, Polyacrylonitrile, Polyvinyl chloride, Polystyrene Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Basic Concepts of Chemistry; General Organic Chemistry.

subjects.name: CHEMICAL ENGINEERING EQUIPMENT DESIGN
subjects.objective: To understand various design of equipment’s used in chemical process industries. To understand various design of equipment used in chemical process industries.
course_outcomes: To Know and understand the various equipments used in the Chemical process Industries.
To Know and understand the flow diagram and block diagram of the chemical process Industries.
To know and understand the various accessories and mounting of chemical engineering equipments.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Various laboratory equipment and devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basic chemical engineering symbols, Laboratory glass ware, instruments and their practice

allSyllabusUnits.title: Block Diagram and Flow diagram

allSyllabusUnits.title: Storage vessels and Pressure vessel
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Types of storage vessel and pressure vessel in detail, Heads, Covers, and Supports

allSyllabusUnits.title: Reaction Vessel

allSyllabusUnits.title: Pumps and Valves

allSyllabusUnits.title: Size reduction equipment
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of size reduction equipments, Jaw crusher, Roll Crusher, Ball mill etc.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Heat Exchanger equipment
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Shell & Tube heat exchanger, Plate & Frame Heat exchangers, Evaporators

allSyllabusUnits.title: Distillation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Simple distillation unit, criteria for selecting distillation operation, Atmospheric and vacuum distillation unit Total Hours 28

The Rigveda is known for hymns; the Samaveda is closely associated with chants and melodies; the Yajurveda contains prose formulas and material related to ritual performance; and the Atharvaveda includes hymns and material concerning everyday life and ritual. [8 marks] Analyze a realistic problem involving the four vedas and their broad roles, such as distinguishing a hymn collection from a collection associated with melodies. Present a reasoned approach, justify key decisions, and state an important limitation or verification check.

[8 marks] Analyze a realistic problem involving purana and itihasa as sources of knowledge and wisdom, such as comparing a narrative tradition and an encyclopaedic work. Present a reasoned approach, justify key decisions, and state an important limitation or verification check.

[8 marks] Analyze a realistic problem involving indian number traditions, measurement, mathematics and jyotisha, such as explaining how calendrical calculations depend on observation and time units. Present a reasoned approach, justify key decisions, and state an important limitation or verification check.
Answers:
Model answer:
Bharatiya Knowledge Systems (BKS) refers to knowledge traditions developed and transmitted in the Indian subcontinent across intellectual, practical, cultural and philosophical fields. Depending on the syllabus framework, areas include Vedic and philosophical literature, language sciences, mathematics, astronomy, medicine, arts, engineering, architecture and environmental practices. Classification helps organize sources and disciplines without treating every tradition as identical. A sound explanation names the field, identifies its historical or textual context, and distinguishes documented practices from later interpretation. Claims should be supported by the relevant text, artifact or historical evidence rather than generalized to all people or periods.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should explain the governing concept, justify the chosen method, check the result and acknowledge a relevant limitation.

Model answer:
The four Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda. The Rigveda is known for hymns; the Samaveda is closely associated with chants and melodies; the Yajurveda contains prose formulas and material related to ritual performance; and the Atharvaveda includes hymns and material concerning everyday life and ritual. Their contents overlap and their textual traditions are complex, so descriptions should be broad rather than absolute. Explain each name and its principal association, and avoid attributing every later scientific or social idea directly to all four Vedas.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should explain the governing concept, justify the chosen method, check the result and acknowledge a relevant limitation.

Model answer:
Purana literature commonly combines cosmology, genealogies, narratives, teachings and accounts of sacred places or practices. Itihasa traditionally refers especially to the Ramayana and Mahabharata and is often studied as narrative literature carrying ethical, political and philosophical reflection. Their purposes and structures differ, but both have been transmitted through layered textual and interpretive traditions. A careful academic discussion identifies the work and passage, distinguishes narrative or normative meaning from independently verified historical fact, and explains how the text has influenced cultural memory, values and interpretation.

A strong answer should explain the governing concept, justify the chosen method, check the result and acknowledge a relevant limitation.

Model answer:
The syllabus connects historical number systems and units for time, distance and weight with arithmetic, geometry, trigonometry, algebra and astronomy. Vedanga Jyotisha concerns calendrical and astronomical timing in a traditional textual setting. Claims about origins or historical priority should be tied to specific evidence. A common presentation counts the four Vedas, six Vedangas and four additional knowledge traditions such as Mimamsa, Nyaya, Purana and Dharmashastra, though descriptions can vary by source. The framework shows how textual study, interpretation, language, ritual, reasoning and normative traditions were organized. The six Vedangas are Shiksha (phonetics/pronunciation), Chandas (metre), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology or explanation of words), Kalpa (ritual procedure) and Jyotisha (astronomical/calendrical timing). A complete answer names the six fields and explains at least one practical role of each instead of confusing them with modern engineering subjects.

Questions: [8 marks] Explain Metallurgy and iron/steel technology in historical India. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Traditional textile technology and dyeing. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Water management and rainwater harvesting. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Sacred ecology, forests and agricultural knowledge. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
Metallurgy includes obtaining metals from ores and shaping or treating them for use. A historical discussion can cover ore preparation, heating and reduction, forging, joining, heat treatment and the properties sought, while recognizing that techniques varied across periods and regions. Iron and steel production requires evidence about the artifact, process and material; the existence of a notable artifact does not prove that one technique was universal. A well-supported answer connects process to properties such as strength, hardness, corrosion behaviour or workability and identifies the limits of the available evidence.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Textile technology includes fibre preparation, spinning, weaving and finishing. Dyeing adds colour using a dye source and a process suited to the fibre; preparation, temperature, time and mordants can affect shade and colour fastness. Historical Indian textile traditions included sophisticated regional practices, but materials and techniques differed. To analyze a process, identify the fibre, colour source, preparation, application and finishing steps, then explain how these steps influence the result. Avoid treating all traditional dyes or textile methods as chemically or historically identical.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Water management combines collection, storage, distribution, drainage and maintenance. Rainwater harvesting captures runoff from a roof or catchment, conveys it through channels, filters or settles sediment, and stores or recharges it where appropriate. Traditional systems were adapted to local rainfall, terrain, materials and community needs; Gujarat and other regions contain different examples. A useful analysis checks catchment area, water demand, overflow, contamination prevention and maintenance responsibility. Historical systems should be explained in their local setting rather than assumed to work unchanged in every modern site.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Traditional ecological knowledge may connect land, water, forests, seasonal cycles and social or religious practices. A study of Nakshatra-related agricultural knowledge should identify the particular calendar or observational claim and compare it with the local context and available evidence. Forest management and sacred natural sites can also be studied for their cultural meaning and practical conservation effects. Do not assume that every community followed one identical practice or that cultural association alone proves a measurable ecological outcome. Distinguish historical description, current practice and independently tested environmental effects.

[8 marks] Explain Planning and organizing an assignment. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
A formal email needs a specific subject line, an appropriate greeting, a concise opening that states the purpose, organized details, a clear request or next step, a courteous closing and the sender's name. Use a professional tone, correct grammar and paragraphs that each serve one purpose. Check the recipient address and any attachment before sending. Add CC only for people who need visibility and BCC when recipients should not see one another's addresses. Do not place confidential information in unnecessary recipients or subject lines.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A formal application identifies the recipient, date, subject and applicant, then states the request clearly and gives only relevant reasons or supporting details. It uses a respectful salutation, concise body paragraphs, a clear closing and the required signature or identification. The writer should maintain a formal tone, avoid slang and emotional exaggeration, and ensure the requested action is explicit. Proofread names, dates and attachments. A good application lets the recipient understand what is being requested, why it is justified and what response or approval is needed.

Questions: [8 marks] Explain Number sets and laws of indices. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain HCF and LCM of integers. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain HCF and LCM of fractions and decimals. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Polynomial definitions and arithmetic operations. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
Number sets include natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, irrational numbers and real numbers, with each set having specific membership rules. For a non-zero base a, powers follow laws such as a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. These laws require attention to conditions such as non-zero denominators and the base not being zero for a^0. For example, 2^3 × 2^4 ÷ 2^5 = 2^(3+4−5) = 2^2 = 4.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
The HCF is the greatest positive integer that divides every given integer; the LCM is the smallest positive common multiple. Prime factorization is a reliable method: 12 = 2^2 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3^2. For HCF, take common prime factors with the smallest exponents, giving 2 × 3 = 6. For LCM, take each prime factor with the greatest exponent, giving 2^2 × 3^2 = 36. For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
First express fractions in their lowest terms. For positive fractions, the usual course rules are HCF = HCF of numerators divided by LCM of denominators, and LCM = LCM of numerators divided by HCF of denominators. Thus for 2/3 and 4/5, HCF = 2/15 and LCM = 4. For decimals, convert values to integers by multiplying by an appropriate power of ten, find the HCF/LCM, then rescale the result. Keep the decimal-place adjustment consistent and verify the resulting multiples or divisors.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A polynomial is an expression formed from constants and variables with non-negative integer exponents and coefficients. Like terms have the same variable part and exponents, so only their coefficients are combined. For example, (2x + 3) + (x − 5) = 3x − 2. The degree of a non-zero polynomial in one variable is the highest exponent with a non-zero coefficient; the degree of 3x^4 − 2x^2 + 7 is four. Keep signs and exponents unchanged while grouping terms, and simplify before identifying the degree.

Model answer:
An algebraic identity is an equality that holds for every permitted value of its variables. Common identities include (a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, (a−b)^2 = a^2 − 2ab + b^2, and (a+b)(a−b) = a^2 − b^2. They support expansion, factorization and simplification. For example, (x+3)^2 = x^2 + 6x + 9. The middle term in a squared binomial is important; omitting it or using the wrong sign is a common error. Substitution can check a result.

Model answer:
Perimeter measures the total distance around a plane figure; area measures the enclosed surface. For a rectangle, perimeter is 2(l+w) and area is lw. For a square, perimeter is 4a and area is a². For a triangle, area is ½ × base × perpendicular height; for a circle, circumference is 2πr and area is πr². Use compatible units, distinguish linear units from square units, and identify the required dimension rather than assuming a sloping side is the perpendicular height. State the formula, substitute values and report units.

For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers.

Answers:
Model answer:
Classify numbers carefully: integers include negative whole-number values, rational numbers can be expressed as a ratio of integers with non-zero denominator, irrational values cannot be so expressed, and real numbers include rational and irrational values. For a non-zero base a, use a^m a^n = a^(m+n), a^m/a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. State domain restrictions and simplify stepwise; exponents add when multiplying like bases and subtract when dividing them.

Model answer:
For integers, prime-factorize and use minimum exponents for HCF and maximum exponents for LCM. For positive fractions in lowest terms, use HCF(numerators)/LCM(denominators) for HCF, and LCM(numerators)/HCF(denominators) for LCM. For decimals, scale all values by the same power of ten to make integers, calculate HCF or LCM, then reverse the scale. Example: HCF(12,18)=6 and LCM(12,18)=36. Check that the HCF divides the original integers and the LCM is a common multiple.

Model answer:
Combine only like terms, preserve signs, and use the highest non-zero exponent to determine degree. Common identities include (a+b)^2=a²+2ab+b², (a−b)^2=a²−2ab+b² and (a+b)(a−b)=a²−b². For example, (x+3)^2=x²+6x+9; the 6x middle term comes from both cross-products. Use identities to expand or factor efficiently, and verify by substitution of a convenient value when checking a potentially incorrect expression.
